title: FAR Module 2 · TBS 5
html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Integrated Balance Sheet Analysis

Analyze year-end information involving bonds payable, investments, treasury stock, and retained earnings.

Scenario

Summit Corp. is preparing its December 31 financial statements. Analyze each of the following independent items.

Item 1 — Bonds Payable

On January 1, Summit issued $500,000 face amount of bonds at par.

The bonds have a 6% annual stated interest rate, with interest paid annually on December 31.

Item 2 — Trading Debt Security

Summit purchased a debt security classified as a trading security for $90,000.

At December 31, its fair value is $98,000.

Assume there are no other adjustments affecting the investment's carrying amount.

Item 3 — Treasury Stock

Summit reacquired 2,000 shares of its own common stock for $15 per share.

Summit uses the cost method for treasury stock.

Item 4 — Retained Earnings

Beginning retained earnings were $420,000.

Summit reports $95,000 of net income for the year and declared cash dividends of $25,000.

Required

1. Annual Bond Interest Expense
2. Unrealized Gain on Trading Security
3. Treasury Stock Balance
4. Ending Retained Earnings
explanation:
Step 1 — Bond Interest

Because the bonds were issued at par, the stated rate equals the effective rate at issuance in this simplified scenario.

$500,000 × 6% = $30,000

Interest Expense: $30,000

Step 2 — Trading Security

Fair Value $98,000 − Carrying Amount $90,000 = $8,000 Unrealized Gain

Because the debt security is classified as trading, the unrealized holding gain is recognized in current-period earnings.

Unrealized Gain: $8,000

Step 3 — Treasury Stock

2,000 Shares × $15 = $30,000

Under the cost method, treasury stock is recorded at the amount paid to reacquire the shares.

Treasury Stock: $30,000

Step 4 — Retained Earnings

Beginning Retained Earnings $420,000 + Net Income $95,000 − Dividends $25,000 = $490,000

Ending Retained Earnings: $490,000

CPA Takeaway

  • Bonds issued at par have no initial premium or discount.
  • Trading debt securities are reported at fair value, with unrealized holding gains and losses recognized in earnings.
  • Treasury stock under the cost method is recorded at reacquisition cost and is a contra-equity account.
  • Net income increases retained earnings, while dividends decrease retained earnings.
